Case reference: 2014001521%%KRYGER, Nath.CaseDesc: On November 3, 1972, a helicopter carrying a pilot and three passengers went missing in Lake Winnipeg. The helicopter left Thompson, Manitoba at 3:20 p.m. and was heading for Winnipeg after stopping at a number of communities. The helicopter landed at Warren's Landing at approximately 5:20 p.m., and left for Winnipeg. The pilot reported that the weather was poor and he estimated his arrival in Winnipeg at 8:00 p.m. At 5:50 p.m. there was radio contact with the pilot where he stated that he was over Poplar River. This was the last radio contact with this helicopter. The Canadian Air Search and Rescue, private aircraft and police aircraft searched until November 17, 1972 when the search was suspended until the spring of 1973. Nathan Kryger and Ian Fraser are presumed dead as a result of the helicopter crash. Foul play is not suspected.
Case reference: 2014001521%%KRYGER, Nath.Name: KRYGER, Nathen David

Case reference: 2014002145%%GARSON, Will.CaseDesc: On September 13, 1975, William Garson, his father, his brother and a friend set out for a hunt in Moose Lake, Manitoba. On September 14, other hunters found gas cans and a thermos with the Garson name on it. These hunters reported their findings to the police.  A search was initiated and police found a boat sitting upright on the bottom of the lake. The depth of the lake around the boat was only 8 to 10 feet. Police believe the men encountered extremely rough water while crossing Moose Lake. The motors were found to be in forward gear. There was no flotation gear in the boat and it was heavily loaded with camping and hunting equipment. All bodies recovered except William, presumed drowned.

The Victoria Police investigated Belinda's disappearance and determined that Belinda suffered from a mental illness, had a drug addiction and may have been a sex trade worker. Fort Churchill's military authorities commenced a search with the aid of helicopters and aircraft. On September 21, the two boats used by the men were located; both were undamaged and swamped. Case reference: 2008000799%%FIELD, James.CaseDesc: On August 26th, 1986 Terry Field and Linda Blackwell left Lost Nation Airport, east of Cleveland, Ohio en route to Brantford Municipal Airport, Brantford, Ontario.  The plane was 18 minutes into its flight when the pilot communicated with Cleveland Air Traffic Control that they were encountering severe turbulence.  They requested new vectors to fly. The pilot was advised to turn west, then Air Traffic Control lost radio and radar contact with the plane. Debris from the plane was located on August 27, 1986 in Lake Erie, approximately 32 nautical miles south of the St.Thomas Airport. Debris was drifting in a southeast direction and was recovered approximately 1-3 nautical miles on the Canadian side of the international boundary line in Lake Erie. Debris was identified by Bud Field,  brother of Terry Field, as having come from the missing aircraft.
Case reference: 2008000799%%FIELD, James.Name: FIELD, James Terry

Case reference: 2014005499%%DESJARLAIS,.CaseDesc: During the early morning hours of Friday, October 1st, 2010, Janice Cher Desjarlais and her boyfriend crawled into a dumpster located behind The Center of Hope on Franklin Avenue in Fort McMurray. When he was unable to find her, he suspected that the dumpster may have been emptied during his absence. Case reference: 2014001522%%STACKHOUSE,.CaseDesc: On July 7, 1977, James Stackhouse and a colleague were camped on a small island on the east shore of Lake Winnipeg, north of Hole River in Manitoba. Their vessel was drifting southwards, approaching Deer Island, which is situated 6 kilometres south of their current position. At approximately 6:00 p.m., the two men departed the shore, each holding onto small logs that had been tied together. They attempted to swim to Deer Island, but strong currents and waves carried them instead to a location east of Deer Island. The improvised raft constructed by the men was compromised, leading to their separation. The friend swam to Deer Island, but unfortunately James was not seen again. Extensive searches of the area were conducted using a variety of methods, including land, air, and water, but the body of James was not recovered.

Case reference: 2014005517%%GUIBOCHE, Am.CaseDesc:
At the time of her disappearance, Amber Guiboche was living in the north end of Winnipeg with her boyfriend and his family. Amber had been leading a high-risk lifestyle.

Amber spent the evening of November 10th, 2010 socializing with friends. Later that evening she went to a friend’s residence on Bushnell St. She left there alone at around 11:45 p.m., and walked to the intersection of Isabel Street and William Ave.  

She was picked up there shortly after by a man driving a burgundy pickup truck. The truck was described as an older, burgundy Chevrolet Silverado, extended cab, short box with a “4x4” decal toward the rear of the box. 

The truck was last seen traveling southbound on Isabel St. It was captured on video in the area in which she was last seen.

Images of this truck and a forensic artist’s sketch of the driver have been made available.
Case reference: 2014005517%%GUIBOCHE, Am.Name: GUIBOCHE, Amber Rosemarie

Case reference: 2014001837%%URSU, Freder.CaseDesc: On September 29, 1979 at approximately 8:30 a.m. seven men departed from Anama Bay, Manitoba on a fishing trip. The men departed as a group in three separate boats and were heading for Warpath. At approximately 7:30 p.m. that same day, the occupants of the first boat reported to the RCMP that the other two boats were missing. They described the waves as being three to four feet high and they could not see the tree line from where they were. They lost sight of the other two boats and fired shotgun shots into the air hoping for a response. No response was received. Extensive patrols by air, boat and land were made in an attempt to locate the remaining five men. The bodies of Fredrick Ursu and Jerry Hudy were never recovered. They are presumed dead due to drowning.

Case reference: 2014003250%%PETAWANAHQUE.CaseDesc: On November 1, 1974, four people left the Whitedog Indian Reserve, Ontario in a 14' Lund boat and were heading for Pointe du Bois, Manitoba. Their intention was to go to Pointe du Bois to pick up supplies and then return to Whitedog. On November 5, 1974, these individuals were reported missing as they had never returned to Whitedog.  It is believed that the boat overturned and everyone drowned. Two bodies were recovered, and the cause of death was determined to be drowning. Searches were conducted by boat and by air but the bodies of Paul Scott and Richard Petawanahqueb were never recovered.  Paul and Richard are presumed dead due to drowning. No foul play is suspected.

Case reference: 2014002108%%WALDUM, Crai.CaseDesc: On August 18, 1978, Craig Waldum took part in a canoeing expedition along the Nelson River in Gillam, Manitoba, with seven other people. He was one of two guides on the trip. Three members of the group were on the riverbank. They were guiding the second canoe to shore with a rope. The remaining five members, including Craig, were in the second canoe. While guiding the canoe to shore, they gave the rope some slack. This caused the bow of the canoe to turn out into the current and tip over. Those on the shore were unable to hold onto the rope because of the strength of the current and the canoe was swept downstream. Craig held onto the canoe for a couple of hours, and then he was seen to let go. He slipped under the water and did not resurface. His remains have not been recovered.

Case reference: 2020011537%%BUTCH, Veron.CaseDesc: On February 11, 1985, Veronica Butch was seen for the last time in Toronto, Ontario. That day, Veronica had moved out of the apartment that she shared with her boyfriend and she was supposed to move in with her sister, but she never arrived.
Case reference: 2020011537%%BUTCH, Veron.Name: BUTCH, Veronica Lynn

Case reference: 1999003370%%LIOU, Nancy.CaseDesc: Nancy Liou was last seen at home on January 27, 1999. On January 28, her father contacted Nancy's school to see if she was there, and was advised they had no way of knowing if she was in attendance as it was exam time. Her father contacted police that evening when she failed to return home from school.  She had advised a family member she was leaving but never said where she was headed.
Case reference: 1999003370%%LIOU, Nancy.Name: LIOU, Nancy

Case reference: 2014004911%%HARPER, Elli.CaseDesc: On July 3, 1974, Ellice Harper, his wife and their young child were out on the lake duck hunting and fishing on Red Sucker Lake, Manitoba. At one point in the day, the party stopped on shore to eat. During this stop, they noticed a storm coming in. By the time they left there were already waves forming as they started out across the lake. The wind increased and the waves were so strong that they would almost cause the vessel to flip over. The boat filled with water and a wave took him out of the boat. His wife and child drifted in the boat until they reached shore and were later rescued. It is presumed Ellice drowned.
Case reference: 2014004911%%HARPER, Elli.Name: HARPER, Ellice

Case reference: 2012020044%%SLOAT, Rodne.CaseDesc: On December 23, 1986, Rodney Sloat was seen for the last time, by his friends, in Strathcona County, Alberta. That evening, Rodney was having dinner at his friends’ residence, and had left on his snowmobile at approximately midnight. During the time of his disappearance, Rodney may have been despondent. All of his personal belongings, identification, and snowmobile were found at his residence.
Case reference: 2012020044%%SLOAT, Rodne.Name: SLOAT, Rodney Leonard

Case reference: 2014005179%%GRIFFIS, Ric.CaseDesc: On September 20, 2006, Richard Griffis was seen for the last time when he went down to the White River in the remote community of Beaver Creek in the Yukon. Richard had been visiting from the United States, and had travelled to the Yukon to test out an outdoor survival suit that he invented.
Case reference: 2014005179%%GRIFFIS, Ric.Name: GRIFFIS, Richard Lyman

Case reference: 2014001612%%LAROSE, Rene.CaseDesc: On July 17, 1975, Renée Larose was seen for the last time when she left her home in the borough of Rosemont-La Petite-Patrie in the city of Montreal, Quebec. No one has seen or heard from her since.
Case reference: 2014001612%%LAROSE, Rene.Name: LAROSE, Renee

Case reference: 2012020070%%THOMAS, Lesl.CaseDesc: Leslie Thomas was reported missing on  December 8, 2000.  He was last seen walking west on Highway 201 in the Roseau River First Nation located south of Winnipeg in Manitoba, during the first week of November 2000.  Leslie's whereabouts remain unknown.
Case reference: 2012020070%%THOMAS, Lesl.Name: THOMAS, Leslie George

Case reference: 2013000113%%DERRICK, Lan.CaseDesc: Lana Derrick was given a ride from Houston, BC where she was going to college, to Terrace where she was dropped off at a friend's house.  Ms. Derrick spent the evening with friends hanging out in the Terrace downtown core.  In the early morning hours of October 7, 1995, Ms. Derrick picked up $30 from a friend's house and was last seen at the Copperside Foods/Petro Canada in Thornhill.  Her family reported her missing three days later when she did not show up for Thanksgiving dinner.
Case reference: 2013000113%%DERRICK, Lan.Name: DERRICK, Lana Patricia

Scar: Cheek, 3 on left side of face
Case reference: 2014003355%%BREW, Kelsey.CaseDesc: Kelsey Brew and his friends were playing on the rocks on the shores of the Hudson Bay in Churchill, Manitoba. According to the witness Kelsey attempted to help another boy who had fallen in the water. As Kelsey was helping, a wave came in and he also slipped into the water. A large number of volunteers walked the shoreline and boat patrols failed to locate him. It is assumed Kelsey drowned.
Case reference: 2014003355%%BREW, Kelsey.Name: BREW, Kelsey Randall

Hair: Brown, Short, Sometimes has a goatee.
Case reference: 2014006316%%MUNRO, Andre.CaseDesc: Andrew William Munro was last seen in Stewart, British Columbia on November 15, 2013. Police and family are concerned for his well being as he needs daily medication. He may be clean shaven or have a goatee. Mr. Munro may have been crossing the border between British Columbia and Alaska. Mr. Munro was a long time lower mainland resident who had recently moved to Stewart, to pursue a career in the logging industry.
Case reference: 2014006316%%MUNRO, Andre.Name: MUNRO, Andrew William

Case reference: 2014002407%%ELLIS, Rober.CaseDesc: On  June 27, 1973, Robert Scott Ellis and a friend went fishing on Reed Lake in Manitoba. They left in the morning around 9:30 a.m. and fished until about 6:00 p.m. when they decided to return home. As the day progressed, the weather deteriorated and the water became quite rough. They began to take on water over the sides of the canoe. Despite the progress they were making, the canoe was finally rolled over by a wave. Both men held on to the canoe for hours, but Robert eventually got tired and let go.  When the friend finally reached shore, he reported the incident. A drag and dive operation was launched, but the results were negative. It is presumed that Robert drowned.
Case reference: 2014002407%%ELLIS, Rober.Name: ELLIS, Robert Scott

Teeth: Visible Missing, First or second molar upper left jaw, gap in front teeth.
Case reference: 2009004199%%SOKPOR, Mano.CaseDesc: Manou Sokpor was reported missing to police by his fiancée. She had last spoken with Manou at 2:00 a.m. on May 14th, 2009 by telephone; nothing seemed out of the ordinary. His fiancée had no further contact with Manou the rest of that day which was out of his character. On May 15th the vehicle Manou usually drove was located in his driveway, and his wallet and cellular phone were in the bedroom.
Case reference: 2009004199%%SOKPOR, Mano.Name: SOKPOR, Manou Kokou

Case reference: 2018000902%%HARVEY, Dani.CaseDesc: Daniel Harvey was seen for the last time on December 28, 2017 in the Bellerive district of Montreal, Quebec. None of Daniel's personal items were missing from his apartment.
Case reference: 2018000902%%HARVEY, Dani.Name: HARVEY, Daniel

Case reference: 2014003138%%SANDERSON, J.CaseDesc: On October 17, 1981, John Sanderson was with some friends in Berens River, Manitoba.  He left in a 22' boat heading for Jackhead, Manitoba.  Friends tried to stop him from leaving due to the high winds but he left anyway. On October 19, 1981, the boat that he had taken was found upside down and partly submerged near the shore of Pigeon Point. Gas cans that had been in the boat were also located.  Searches were done by air and water but the body of John was never found. It is presumed that Mr. Sanderson drowned.
Case reference: 2014003138%%SANDERSON, J.Name: SANDERSON, John Henry

Deformity: Abdomen, excess skin due to weigh lost
Scar: Abdomen, operation on abdomen for weight loss
Case reference: 2012020130%%MARABELLA, M.CaseDesc:
Mario Marabella, 40 years old, was on his way to a meeting when he was abducted on December 4, 2008 in Laval, Quebec.  Mario was at a Petro-Canada service station on Highway 440 between highways 19 and 25 around 4:00 p.m. when three people forced him into a van and fled. 

Mario's car, a grey Acura MDX, was retrieved around 8:00 p.m. that evening by one or more of the abductors at the same Petro-Canada station from which he was abducted. A few hours later the car was found burning at the corner of Gouin Boulevard and Lambert St. in Montréal, Quebec.  Mario was linked to the Italian Mafia and was known to be involved in organized crime.
Case reference: 2012020130%%MARABELLA, M.Name: MARABELLA, Mario

Hair: Grey, Long, Unkempt; unkempt Beard, Moustache
Deformity: leg, walks with a pronounced limp
Case reference: 2008015999%%ZUERN, John.CaseDesc: John Zuern went missing on June 14,1975, from the London Psychiatric Hospital in London, Ontario. He’s been diagnosed as schizophrenic and walks with a pronounced limp.  John’s brother reported seeing him in the Bloor and Spadina area of Toronto during the summer of 1980.  He was believed to have been living on the streets at the time.
Case reference: 2008015999%%ZUERN, John.Name: ZUERN, John Walter

Case reference: 2021006090%%FOWLER, Jona.CaseDesc: At the end of July, 2019, Jonathan Fowler was seen for the last time in Picton, Ontario. Since then, there has not been any activity on his banking, phone and social media accounts. During the time of his disappearance, Jonathan was engaged in a high risk lifestyle.
Case reference: 2021006090%%FOWLER, Jona.Name: FOWLER, Jonathan Daniel
